findings.title: HTML inside MessageFormat choice branches is never sanitized
findings.body: normalizeValue() replaces each complete {n,choice,...} expression with "..." before the OWASP sanitizer runs. Consequently, markup placed in a choice branch for keys such as linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.* or error-invalid-multivalued-size is never inspected: for example a branch containing a script or malicious anchor passes verification if the rest of the value passes, but MessageFormat can select and output that branch at runtime. The verifier should check the text of each choice alternative after removing only the choice syntax and comparison operators, rather than discarding the whole expression.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax breaks Account UI interpolation
findings.body: This Account UI resource uses i18next-style double-brace placeholders ({{0}}, {{1}}, etc.) throughout the file, but error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed to Java MessageFormat syntax: {0}, {1}, and {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. i18next does not evaluate MessageFormat choice expressions, so this value will render literal or unresolved placeholders instead of the interpolated limits and pluralized noun. Keep the UI resource in its double-brace/value(s) form and handle that form in the verifier instead.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax breaks Admin UI interpolation
findings.body: As in the other React UI resources, this file previously used i18next-style {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} placeholders for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but it was changed to Java MessageFormat {0}/{1}/{2,choice,...}. The Admin UI's i18next interpolation does not evaluate MessageFormat choice expressions, so the formatted error can show literal placeholders instead of the attribute limits. The Java choice form belongs only in the server-side theme properties, not in this UI resource.

findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian account message totpStep1 now reads "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, replacing the previous Lithuanian sentence. Lithuanian users will see setup instructions in the wrong language. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:" without the removed anchor tags.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 now reads "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, replacing the previous Lithuanian sentence. Lithuanian users will see TOTP setup instructions in the wrong language during login. Replace it with the Lithuanian translation of the anchor-free English sentence.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file now uses Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: The new totpStep1 text "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) in the messages_zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) file. It should use the Simplified Chinese equivalent, e.g. "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：", to match the locale.

findings.title: Anchor mismatch error does not identify the file or key
findings.body: santizeAnchors() receives the message key but never uses it, and the added message only says "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string". Unlike the Illegal HTML message, it contains neither the key nor the file. When the verifier runs over hundreds of properties files and thousands of keys, a translator cannot locate the offending entry from this message. Include the key and file in the anchor-mismatch message.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart aborts verification with an unchecked exception
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by rewriting the locale suffix and throws a raw RuntimeException if that derived file cannot be read. verify() only converts IOException to MojoExecutionException and callers otherwise receive collected message strings, so a properties file without a matching _en counterpart (or with a differently named English locale) aborts the whole verification run and masks all other results instead of producing a locatable verification/build error for that file.

findings.title: No positive test that legitimate HTML and anchors pass verification
findings.body: All new sanitizer tests assert that violations are reported; none asserts an empty result for a valid translation that uses allowed HTML (p/strong/b/br) when the English source contains HTML, or for a translation reusing the exact English anchor. A regression that strips or flags all allowed markup, or breaks the anchor-removal logic so legitimate translations always fail, would still pass this suite. Add clean English/translation fixtures expecting no messages.
